name: dpill
title: Select a Bandwidth for Local Linear Regression

origin.description: Uses direct plug-in methodology to select the bandwidth of a local linear Gaussian kernel regression estimate, as described by Ruppert, Sheather and Wand (1995).
origin.usage:
dpill(x, y, blockmax = 5, divisor = 20, trim = 0.01,
      proptrun = 0.05, gridsize = 401L, range.x, truncate = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric vector of x data. Missing values are not accepted.

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: Numeric vector of y data, the same length as x. Missing values are not accepted.

arguments.name: blockmax
arguments.text: Maximum number of blocks used to construct an initial parametric estimate.

arguments.name: divisor
arguments.text: The sample size is divided by this value to set a lower limit on the number of blocks.

arguments.name: trim
arguments.text: Proportion of the sample trimmed from each end in the x direction before the plug-in rule is applied.

arguments.name: proptrun
arguments.text: Proportion of the range of x truncated at each end in the functional estimates.

arguments.name: gridsize
arguments.text: Number of equally spaced grid points over which the function is estimated.

arguments.name: range.x
arguments.text: Minimum and maximum values of x at which to compute the estimate.

arguments.name: truncate
arguments.text: If TRUE, data outside range.x are ignored.

origin.details: Unknown functionals in the expression for the asymptotically optimal bandwidth are replaced by kernel estimates. The kernel is the standard normal density. Least squares quartic fits over blocks of data give an initial estimate, and Mallows' Cp selects the number of blocks.
origin.example:
if(length(data(geyser, package="MASS"))) {
x <- geyser$duration
y <- geyser$waiting
plot(x, y)
h <- dpill(x, y)
fit <- locpoly(x, y, bandwidth = h)
lines(fit)
}

translation.description: Uses direct plug-in methodology to select the bandwidth of a local linear Gaussian kernel regression estimate, as described by Ruppert, Sheather and Wand (1995).
translation.usage:
dpill(x, y, blockmax=5, divisor=20, trim=0.01,
      proptrun=0.05, gridsize=401, range_x=None, truncate=True)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: One-dimensional numeric predictor. Missing values are not accepted.

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: One-dimensional numeric response, the same length as x. Missing values are not accepted.

arguments.name: blockmax
arguments.text: Maximum number of blocks used to construct an initial parametric estimate.

arguments.name: divisor
arguments.text: The sample size is divided by this value to set a lower limit on the number of blocks.

arguments.name: trim
arguments.text: Proportion of the sample trimmed from each end in the x direction before the plug-in rule is applied.

arguments.name: proptrun
arguments.text: Proportion of the range of x truncated at each end in the functional estimates.

arguments.name: gridsize
arguments.text: Number of equally spaced grid points over which the function is estimated.

arguments.name: range_x
arguments.text: Minimum and maximum values of x at which to compute the estimate. This is range.x in R. None uses the minimum and maximum of the trimmed sample.

arguments.name: truncate
arguments.text: If true, data outside range_x are ignored.

translation.details: Unknown functionals in the expression for the asymptotically optimal bandwidth are replaced by kernel estimates. The kernel is the standard normal density. Pairs are binned with the rlbin crate. Least squares quartic fits over blocks of data, from the blkest and cp crates, give an initial estimate, and Mallows' Cp selects the number of blocks. The pilot regression curves are locpoly. The smoother diagonals are sdiag and sstdiag, which invert the local moment matrices with linpack.
translation.example:
from mass import geyser
from kernsmooth.dpill import dpill
from kernsmooth import locpoly
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

x = geyser["duration"]
y = geyser["waiting"]
plt.scatter(x, y)
h = dpill(x, y)
fit = locpoly(x, y, bandwidth=h)
plt.plot(fit["x"], fit["y"])
